notes.meaning: Cyrus king of Persia announced throughout his kingdom that the Jewish exiles could return home, fulfilling what the Lord had promised through the prophet Jeremiah. God showed His supreme control over world leaders by moving the heart of a foreign emperor to carry out His divine plan. God always keeps His promises right on time.

Cyrus announced that the God of heaven had granted him dominion over the earth and charged him to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. God had named Cyrus long before in prophecy, and Cyrus recognized that his imperial success came from heaven. Persian rulers often honored local gods to win the loyalty of conquered peoples, but God used this royal decree to restore His worship.

Cyrus gave full permission and his royal blessing to any of God's people who wished to travel back to Judah and rebuild the temple. Returning was voluntary, inviting those with true devotion to step out in faith. Cyrus recognized the Lord as the true God whose dwelling was tied to Jerusalem.

The king commanded that those who remained behind should give silver, gold, supplies, and animals to support those making the journey. Rebuilding the temple was expensive, so those who stayed were to give freewill offerings to fund the work. Even when believers cannot go somewhere in person, they can still support God's work with their resources.

The heads of families from Judah and Benjamin, together with the priests and Levites, got ready to make the long trip to Jerusalem. Leaving comfortable lives in Babylon for a ruined city was difficult, so only those whose hearts God moved were willing to go. Any good desire to serve the Lord begins with God's grace working within us.

The neighbors gave the travelers silver, gold, goods, livestock, and precious items, in addition to voluntary gifts for the temple. God moved the hearts of both Jewish neighbors who stayed behind and local Gentiles to help those who were leaving. When God calls His people to an assignment, He provides what they need through others.

King Cyrus brought out the holy temple articles that King Nebuchadnezzar had stolen from Jerusalem decades earlier and kept in pagan temples. God had safely preserved these precious worship vessels even while they were stored away in a foreign land. God never forgets what belongs to Him.

Cyrus ordered his royal treasurer to count out the sacred items and place them in the care of Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah. This careful handover ensured that the holy objects were fully protected and entrusted to a recognized leader among God's people. Sheshbazzar was appointed by the crown to lead the returning community home.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars treat Sheshbazzar and Zerubbabel as two separate leaders who served consecutive terms as governor, rather than one person with two different names.

notes.meaning: A detailed inventory lists hundreds of valuable gold and silver dishes, basins, and other utensils used in temple worship. Keeping a careful count showed how highly these consecrated tools were valued after years in exile. God cares about order and faithfulness in every detail of His worship.

Sheshbazzar carried all 5,400 gold and silver articles along as the exiles journeyed from Babylon to Jerusalem. The larger total includes smaller items along with the major pieces listed in the earlier inventory. This great return marked a turning point in history, as God brought His people and their sacred treasures back to the Promised Land.
